newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy hard-left says local vote gives it more power.
newsitem.headline: Italy hard-left says local vote gives it more power.

text.p: The good showing by Communist Refoundation in Sunday's local elections will strengthen the party's hand in coming negotiations on welfare reform, Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said on Monday.

"Given that we got so many votes, this will give more importance to both our social spending and structural reform position -- a position which says social reform will happen but without cuts to spending," Bertinotti told Reuters television.
Refoundation polled almost 10 percent of the vote in the first round of mayoral elections in the key northern cities of Milan and Turin.

Centre-left candidates trailed the opposition centre-right in both votes and the government Olive Tree coalition will need the backing of hard-left supporters if they are to win the second round run-offs, scheduled for May 11.
Bertinotti said any election pact would first require a convergence between Refoundation and the government on the issue of social spending.
"If we reach a clear agreement, we will be able to go to Milan and Turin and other cities and win," Bertinotti said.

"We propose to the Olive Tree, given that where we stand together we win and where they go alone as in Milan and Turin they lose, to correct this error and conclude a partnership with Refoundation...in order to win in the second round," he said.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said he will start an overview of welfare spending by the middle of next month.
Many economists have urged the government to introduce structural cuts to social spending to boost Italy's chances of being in the first wave of countries signing up to the single European currency.
Sunday's elections, in which about one-fifth of the national electorate was eligible, constituted the first ballot box text for Prodi's one-year old coalition government.
